tagline: From Bellingham up the North Fork to Artist Point.
intro: SR 542 leaves Bellingham along Squalicum Creek and heads out through farmland and wooded hills, crosses the Nooksack River and runs through Deming, a town with its roots in logging. At Kendall it turns up the North Fork of the Nooksack, enters the national forest at Glacier and climbs the northeast side of Mount Baker, past the ski area and around Picture Lake, over Austin Pass to Artist Point at 5,210 feet.

It began in 1893 as a county wagon road to Maple Falls and reached Heather Meadows in 1926. For years the snow shut the top each winter, until the filming of The Call of the Wild in 1934 got the highway department plowing.

moments.title: Nooksack Falls
moments.text: Two-thirds of a mile off the highway the North Fork drops 88 feet into a rocky canyon, the falls that turn up in the hunting scene of The Deer Hunter.

moments.title: Picture Lake
moments.text: The highway splits to go around both sides of the lake, which reflects snow-capped Mount Shuksan, its name taken from a Lummi word said to mean high peak.

moments.title: Artist Point
moments.text: The highway ends in a parking lot on Kulshan Ridge, with trails out from it and Mount Baker's 10,781-foot peak across the way.

practical: The last stretch beyond the ski area to Artist Point is closed to vehicles through the snow season and reopens each summer, so check its status before going.
